body_es: AWS CloudFormation es el servicio de Infraestructura como Código (IaC) nativo de AWS que permite aprovisionar y gestionar recursos de AWS mediante plantillas declarativas en formato JSON o YAML. Las plantillas tienen secciones estándar: Parameters (entradas dinámicas), Mappings (tablas de búsqueda), Conditions (lógica condicional), Resources (obligatoria, define los recursos AWS), Outputs (valores exportables) y Metadata. Las plantillas se despliegan como Stacks; CloudFormation gestiona el ciclo de vida completo de los recursos: creación, actualización y eliminación atómica. Los Nested Stacks permiten modularizar plantillas complejas anidando stacks hijos referenciados con AWS::CloudFormation::Stack. Las StackSets extienden los stacks a múltiples cuentas y regiones AWS de forma centralizada, ideal para despliegues de landing zones multi-cuenta. El Drift Detection identifica recursos que han sido modificados fuera de CloudFormation. Los Change Sets permiten previsualizar los cambios antes de aplicarlos, crítico para producción. Las Deletion Policies (Retain, Snapshot, Delete) controlan qué ocurre con los recursos al eliminar un stack. Para el SAA-C03, CloudFormation es la solución cuando se requiere IaC nativa de AWS con gestión de estado integrada, especialmente en arquitecturas multi-cuenta con AWS Organizations. AWS CDK (Cloud Development Kit) genera plantillas CloudFormation usando lenguajes de programación estándar como Python, TypeScript o Java. Terraform, de HashiCorp —no un servicio de AWS—, es la alternativa open source más usada a CloudFormation: usa su propio lenguaje declarativo (HCL) y es compatible con múltiples nubes, no solo AWS.
body_en: AWS CloudFormation is the native Infrastructure as Code (IaC) service for AWS, enabling you to model and provision your entire cloud infrastructure using declarative JSON or YAML templates. Templates follow a structured schema: Parameters (runtime inputs with type validation), Mappings (static lookup tables, e.g., AMI IDs by region), Conditions (logical branches), Resources (the only required section — defines every AWS resource), Outputs (exported values for cross-stack references), and Metadata. Templates are deployed as Stacks; CloudFormation handles creation, update, and deletion atomically with rollback on failure. Nested Stacks compose complex architectures from reusable component stacks referenced via AWS::CloudFormation::Stack. StackSets deploy a single template across multiple AWS accounts and regions from a central administrator account, ideal for multi-account governance and compliance baselines. Change Sets preview the impact of template changes before execution — critical for production environments to assess resource replacements. DeletionPolicy attributes (Retain, Snapshot, Delete) control resource fate when a stack is deleted. Drift Detection identifies manually made resource changes that diverge from the template. For SAA-C03: CloudFormation is the answer for native AWS IaC; understand the difference between update Replace (destroys and recreates the resource) vs. in-place update. AWS CDK generates CloudFormation templates from high-level constructs written in TypeScript, Python, Java, or C#, improving developer productivity. Terraform, from HashiCorp — not an AWS service — is the most widely used open-source alternative to CloudFormation: it uses its own declarative language (HCL) and supports multiple clouds, not just AWS.
example_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Simple EC2 instance with security group
Parameters:
  InstanceType:
    Type: String
    Default: t3.micro
Resources:
  MySecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Enable HTTP
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 80
          ToPort: 80
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
  MyEC2Instance:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Instance
    Properties:
      ImageId: ami-0abcdef1234567890
      InstanceType: !Ref InstanceType
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref MySecurityGroup
Outputs:
  InstanceId:
    Value: !Ref MyEC2Instance
  PublicIP:
    Value: !GetAtt MyEC2Instance.PublicIp
